claims.statement: The reusable `_test.yml` workflow validates required JSON matrix inputs before expanding a non-fail-fast build matrix, then checks out code, uses the local uv setup action, synchronizes the test group, runs platform-specific unit-test commands, and verifies a clean working tree.

`_test.yml` reads maintainer bypass labels from the live GitHub API only for pull-request runs and fails closed if that lookup fails; `ci:allow-warnings` adds `-W default`, while the narrowly scoped release ripgrep bypass can tolerate an install failure and record an artifact without weakening push or merge-group enforcement.

The `✅ CI Success` gate runs trusted base-ref gate logic, always requires lockfile validation, requires scheduled text hygiene, and permits only failed Talon jobs on qualifying non-Talon-source pull requests to be waived with advisory reporting; merge-group evaluation remains strict while push cancellations are tolerated.

`ci.yml` selects package lint/test jobs from path filters for pull requests and merge-group runs while running them all on pushes to `main`; filters include CI infrastructure and editable SDK dependencies, and CI ends in a single `✅ CI Success` gate.

CI unconditionally calls the reusable lockfile workflow, which performs a credential-less checkout and checks every discovered package lockfile when invoked without paths; a separate non-push text-hygiene job runs `make -C libs hygiene` for the PR or merge-group range, and either control blocks the shared gate.

The lockfile checker limits explicit-path validation to owning package directories, expands changed manifests through transitive local `[tool.uv.sources]` consumers, and reports a package-specific relock command when `uv lock --check` fails.

For a trusted release-bot changelog-only curated-notes apply, CI skips normal package work only after finding a conclusive parent CI result, then passes its gate only for an inherited successful parent and preserves a failed parent as a failed gate; a read-only best-effort diagnostic reports sanitized parent-suite failure details without changing that result.

The release-please fan-out detector derives managed components and bump-worthy title types from trusted configuration, excludes each package's configured excluded files such as tests and `uv.lock`, and reports multi-component release-relevant edits; the workflow blocks those results unless the exact acknowledgement label is present.

`check_pr_scope_files.py` derives title-scope and changed-directory package identity from the labeler configuration, ignores lockfile churn, and limits its release-shaped exception to a fully allowlisted set of release artifacts; malformed configuration exits with a failing status rather than producing a clean result.

The PR scope-file workflow runs trusted base-revision detector/configuration against PR-title and API-derived changed-file inputs, fails closed on incomplete lists or invalid detector output, and makes `ci:allow-scope-mismatch` an explicit passing acknowledgement with a sticky release-fan-out consequence warning.

The CI label taxonomy defines `ci:*` labels as human acknowledgements or overrides read by gates; `ci:allow-scope-mismatch` and `ci:allow-lockfile-release` respectively acknowledge scope/path mismatch and multi-package release scope, while the latter label name predates lockfile exclusion.

The release fan-out bypass-warning workflow is advisory rather than load-bearing: it serializes per-PR updates, reads live labels to handle label-event races, and maintains a sticky warning naming touched release components while either fan-out acknowledgement label remains.

The post-merge release-please fan-out watch uses full `main` history and tags to detect managed components whose delta since their manifest-derived release tag contains no release-relevant files, then flags only matching open release-please branches; it is advisory and skips a component temporarily when its release tag is not published.

The dispatch-only release workflow validates normal release SHA and version integrity, isolates read-only artifact building from checksum-verified OIDC publishing, treats `release` environment selection as deployment configuration whose external protections and trusted-publisher registrations must be configured separately, and keeps notes fail-open while guarding release-PR label transitions.

The release-notes job checks out full history at the validated release SHA but obtains `build_release_notes.py` from the workflow revision, passes resolved release metadata to the helper, and deliberately does not make note generation a prerequisite for PyPI publication or GitHub release creation.

`build_release_notes.py` is a dependency-free local recovery helper that resolves reachable predecessor tags with distinct stable and prerelease rules, reads the changelog at the release SHA, bounds package-scoped git-log and contributor lookups, and emits diagnostics when release-note attribution is incomplete.

The release workflow's currently disabled integration-test step retains package-conditional provider-secret wiring, while the documented `release` environment intentionally has no provider credentials until that step is re-enabled.
